item.title: Configuring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) with Spring Security: Multiple Solutions
item.description:
“Configuring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) with Spring Security: Multiple Solutions”

When deploying web applications, especially those involving separate frontend and backend services, encountering Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) restrictions is frequent. Browsers enforce these policies for security, which is why tools like curl might work while browser-initiated AJAX requests fail. If you are using Spring Security, you must explicitly configure CORS support to prevent Spring Security from blocking these requests before they reach Spring MVC handlers.

item.title: Spring Boot: Configuring Multiple Data Sources Explained
item.description:
“Spring Boot: Configuring Multiple Data Sources Explained”

The core challenge lies in defining each data source, differentiating them within the Spring application context, and, crucially, managing transactions across them if necessary. Spring Boot, with its auto-configuration capabilities, simplifies much of this, but specific configurations are key.

Strategies for Multiple Data Source Configuration

Several accepted solutions provide distinct methods for integrating multiple data sources into a Spring Boot project.

Solution 1: Basic Multiple Oracle Data Source Configuration

This approach focuses on configuring two Oracle data sources by defining properties in application.properties and creating @Bean definitions for each.

item.title: Fixing Postgres Connection Refused in Dockerized Spring Apps
item.description:
“Fixing Postgres Connection Refused in Dockerized Spring Apps”

When deploying a Spring application alongside a PostgreSQL database using Docker and docker-compose, developers frequently encounter an error indicating the connection to localhost:5432 is refused. This issue arises because each Docker container operates within its own isolated network namespace. Consequently, localhost inside the application container refers to itself, not the host machine or the separate database container.

How does one correctly configure the Spring application’s data source URL to resolve to the PostgreSQL container service name within the docker-compose network?
